rationale_summary: The AI RMF Roadmap is dominantly framed around innovation_enablement, setting out a flexible, voluntary, internationally aligned program of standards crosswalks, TEVV tools, profiles, case studies, and tutorials to close knowledge gaps and equip organizations to deploy trustworthy AI. Innovation_enablement leads consumer_public_safety, which is a strong secondary frame focused on reducing real-world negative impacts and harms to individuals, groups, communities, and society via TEVV, risk tolerances, and human-AI oversight. Fundamental_rights appears as a secondary rationale through the explicit 'rights-preserving' orientation and sectoral profile priorities covering hiring, criminal justice, and lending.

evidence_spans.quote: Work described in the Roadmap is intended to help fill gaps in knowledge, practice, or guidance and be useful to a broader audience in pursuit of trustworthy and responsible AI.

The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector specific, and use-case agnostic, providing flexibility to organizations of all sizes and in all sectors and throughout society to implement the approaches in the Framework.
NIST intends to investigate how human-AI teams should best be configured to reduce likelihood of negative impacts/harms to individuals, groups, communities, and society.

NIST will work with the broader community to develop tools, benchmarks, testbeds, and standardized methodologies for evaluating risks in AI and system trustworthiness, including from a socio-technical lens.
